summary: Settings › Holidays stops being an empty form. A new provider port (abstract class as the DI token, a `nager` HTTPS driver and a `fake` driver) fetches a country's public holidays for a year; a new sourcing service resolves the organization's sourced country set (every active member's resolved holiday country, plus the organization's own behind a stored checkbox), imports each unsourced country once, records the import in a new `HolidayImport` table, and never overwrites or deletes a `Holiday` row. Three new columns land on `Holiday` (`source`, `externalKey`, `importedAt`) and one new settings table (`OrganizationHolidaySourcing`) holds the checkbox. A new summary route answers days per country, days per person, and — only for a caller holding `view-amounts-owed` — money per person and per currency, valued with the exact Amounts Owed arithmetic (`resolveRateAtDate` + `buildHolidayRow` from `packages/validation`, per-holiday cent rounding then summed) so the two screens cannot disagree. The shipped list route gains a `sourcing` block and a `source` field per row; the screen syncs itself on load, warns about countries it could not source, and draws the summary above the list. Nothing about how a holiday is applied changes: every imported row is an ordinary `Holiday` row to the calendar, the reports and the Time Tracking markers.

tasks.title: Schema: three columns on Holiday, two new tables, one additive migration
detail: Holiday gains `source String @default("manual")`, `externalKey String?`, `importedAt DateTime?` — a documented string column, not a Prisma enum, matching the role/status convention already used on `VacationReserveTransaction.type` (apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma:720).
New model `HolidayImport` exactly as the contracts Data Model states, with `@@unique([organizationId, countryCode, year])` — invariant 3 is enforced by the index, not by the service.

New model `OrganizationHolidaySourcing` with `organizationId String @unique`, `includeOrgCountry Boolean @default(true)`, `updatedAt`, `updatedByAccountId` (FK → Account). A missing row reads as `includeOrgCountry: true`, so there is NO backfill.
Both new tables cascade from Organization; add the back-relations on `Organization` and `Account` that Prisma requires.

One migration directory, `20260907xxxxxx_time_off_02_holiday_sourcing`, written in the style of apps/api/prisma/migrations/20260904120000_time_off_01_vacation_calendar/migration.sql: a header comment saying why it is additive and what the deploy order makes safe.
Run `npx prisma migrate dev` FROM apps/api — from the repository root the generated client cannot find apps/api/.env.

migration.note: Strictly additive: two CREATE TABLEs and three ADD COLUMNs, all nullable or defaulted, no rename, no drop, no new NOT NULL on an existing table, no backfill. infra/deploy.sh runs `prisma migrate deploy` on the NEW image BEFORE the Terraform rollout of the services (infra/deploy.sh:27 and the comment block at infra/deploy.sh:27-41), so the new schema is in place before any code that names these columns starts serving; because the change is additive the reverse order — the previous image against this schema — is also safe, which is why a code rollback needs no database rollback.

concurrency.lock: none is added. Holiday already carries `@@unique([organizationId, date, countryCode])` plus a hand-written partial index for the two-globals-on-one-date case (see the mapDuplicate comment at apps/api/src/holidays/holidays.service.ts), and that index — not a lock — is what makes Edge case 12 (two admins syncing the same unsourced year) safe. HolidayImport's `@@unique([organizationId, countryCode, year])` plays the same role for invariant 3.

tasks.title: The holiday provider port, the nager driver, the fake driver, and configuration
detail: `HolidayProvider` is an abstract class used as its own DI token — the shape `CalendarProvider` and `Storage` already have (apps/api/src/app.module.ts:132-159). One method: `holidaysFor(countryCode, year): Promise<ProviderHoliday[]>`, where a `ProviderHoliday` carries `date`, `name`, `countryCode`, `global`, `counties`, `types` — the fields the Observations table recorded live.

The port's contract for failure: the method THROWS on a refused connection, a non-conforming status, an unparseable body or a timeout, and RESOLVES with `[]` for a covered country with no holidays. That single distinction is what separates REQ-02-009 (write nothing, report unsourced) from REQ-02-010 (write a record with a count of zero). Say it in the port's docstring — a driver that collapses the two makes the service re-ask forever.

`nager` driver: `GET {base}/api/v3/PublicHolidays/{year}/{code}` over HTTPS, no credential, no header identifying the organization, the account or the deployment (§Security). Bound the call the way apps/api/src/signature/signwell/signwell-http-client.ts:608-620 does — an `AbortController` with a `setTimeout`, cleared in a `finally`; Node's global fetch has no timeout of its own. Default base `https://date.nager.at`, default bound from `HOLIDAY_PROVIDER_TIMEOUT_MS`.

Entry filtering happens in the DRIVER, and it is where Validation Rules 4–7 run (contracts §Boundary values names the driver as the conversion point for every one of them): keep `global === true` and `types` containing `Public` (REQ-02-005); parse `date` as a date-only value, never through a zone-bearing `Date`, and drop one outside the requested year (Rule 4); uppercase and compare `countryCode` to the one requested (Rule 5); take the ENGLISH `name`, not `localName`, and run `validateHolidayName` on it (Rule 6). The driver returns the survivors AND the number it refused, so the service can report `discarded` — a driver that silently drops them leaves REQ-02-022 uncountable.

`fake` driver: seeded fixtures keyed by country, and it must reproduce all six behaviours of the contracts table — Poland's all-nationwide shape, Germany's 10-of-20 mixed shape, an empty answer for a covered country, a hard failure, a call that never answers, and an entry with a 200-character name plus one dated outside the requested year. Give it setters an integration test can drive AND a deterministic default map for the E2E run (a country the fake answers, a country it fails, a country it answers empty), because an E2E test cannot reach into the process to seed it.
The fake counts its own calls — TC-02-INT-02 and TC-02-INT-06 assert the driver was called zero times on the second sync.

Selection follows the mail idiom (apps/api/src/mail/mail.provider.ts): an explicit `HOLIDAY_PROVIDER` of `nager` or `fake` always wins; unset means `fake` whenever `NODE_ENV` is not `production`, and `nager` in production. An unknown value throws at boot, the way resolveCalendarConfig does (apps/api/src/hiring/calendar/calendar.config.ts:44-52), so a typo cannot silently disable sourcing.
apps/api/.env.example gains HOLIDAY_PROVIDER, HOLIDAY_PROVIDER_BASE_URL and HOLIDAY_PROVIDER_TIMEOUT_MS with the comment style the file already uses. None is a secret; none goes to SSM.

tasks.title: Sourcing service: the country set, the import, the import records, the setting
detail: `sourcedCountrySet(organizationId)`: read every ACTIVE membership's `countryCode` and the organization's `countryCode`, read the sourcing setting (a missing row reads `includeOrgCountry: true`), and hand all of it to `resolveSourcedCountrySet` from T2. Scoped by `session.organizationId`, never by the path parameter.

`countryStates(organizationId, year)`: for every country in the set, the import record if one exists → `sourced` / `empty`, else `unsourced`, plus `holidayCount` and `lastImportedAt`. This is what the list route's `sourcing` block and the sync response both report; write it once.

`sync(session, { year, refresh })`: gate on `manage-holidays` (404, never 403 — REQ-02-020) via `can(normalizeRole(membership.role), 'manage-holidays')`; validate `year` with T2's rule (422 `yearInvalid`); then for each country in the set: skip it when an import record exists and `refresh` is false (REQ-02-007 — and the driver must not be called at all, which TC-02-INT-02 asserts by call count); otherwise call the provider.

On a provider THROW: catch per country, log, write NO holiday and NO import record, report that country `unsourced`, and keep going — the route answers 200 whatever any country did (REQ-02-009, TC-02-INT-05, TC-02-INT-14). One country's failure never aborts another's write.

On a provider ANSWER: for each surviving entry create a `Holiday` with the provider's English name, its date, the country's uppercase alpha-2, `paidHours` 8.00, `source: "imported"`, `externalKey` `{provider}:{countryCode}:{date}`, `importedAt` now (REQ-02-004). Before writing, check for a row already on that (organizationId, date, countryCode) — present → write nothing and count `skipped` (REQ-02-006, whatever put it there: manual or imported). ALSO catch P2002 around each create and count it as `skipped`: two admins syncing at once is Edge case 12, and the unique index is what makes the loser's write collide rather than duplicate.

Counting (REQ-02-022): `written` = rows created; `skipped` = entries a row already held the date and country for; `discarded` = entries the driver refused under REQ-02-005 or Validation Rules 4–6. The decision table in the spec is the whole truth table — a regional entry is DISCARDED whether or not a row exists on its date, and the existing row is neither consulted nor touched.

Then upsert the `HolidayImport` for (organizationId, countryCode, year) with the provider name, the moment, and the count (REQ-02-021), catching P2002 on the create half and applying it as an update so Edge case 12 leaves exactly one record. An empty answer writes a record with a count of zero (REQ-02-010) and is never re-asked without refresh (TC-02-INT-06).
**Read the blocking finding P1 before writing the state derivation.** `holidayCount` after a refresh that writes nothing is what the spec contradicts itself about; do not resolve it here.

`getSetting(session)` / `putSetting(session, body)` for GET and PUT `/settings/holiday-sourcing`: `view-holidays` on the read and `manage-holidays` on the write, both 404 (REQ-02-019, REQ-02-020); the body carries exactly `includeOrgCountry` and nothing else, validated by T2's rule (422 `includeOrgCountryInvalid`) — absent or non-boolean is refused, never coerced. Upsert the row whole, no read-modify-write, no lock, the reasoning the neighbouring OrganizationCountryService states verbatim (apps/api/src/organizations/organization-country.service.ts:36-41). Record `updatedByAccountId` from the session.
Never delete a Holiday row and never modify one whose `source` is `manual` — invariants 1 and 2, and they hold under every state and event including refresh.

tasks.title: The summary: days by country, days by person, and the money — the report's arithmetic, not a second one
detail: `GET /holidays/summary`'s body, gated on `view-holidays` → 404 otherwise (REQ-02-019), `year` validated by T2's rule → 422 `yearInvalid`.

**Split the method in two**: the route handler resolves the caller and the two capabilities, and a second method takes the organization id, the year and an explicit `canViewAmounts` flag. TC-02-INT-11 drives that second method directly, because no shipped role holds `view-holidays` without `view-amounts-owed` — the cases file says so and the Known Gaps table records it. Without the split the case cannot be written at all.

`countries[]`: one row per country in the sourced country set (T4's builder), carrying `countryCode`, `holidayCount` and `memberCount` = how many ACTIVE members resolve to it. See the note on globals in `risks` — count a holiday toward a country when `isHolidayApplicableToMember` would apply it to a member of that country (its `countryCode` is null or equal), which is the one rule this area already uses and the only one that keeps a country's row and its members' rows agreeing on the same screen.

`members[]`: one row per ACTIVE membership — `membershipId`, `displayName` (`${firstName} ${lastName}`.trim(), the shape reports.service.ts:1057 builds), the RESOLVED `countryCode` (`resolveMemberHolidayCountry`), `holidayCount` = the holidays that reach them via `isHolidayApplicableToMember`, `paidHours` = the sum of those holidays' `paidHours` as a two-decimal string.

Money (REQ-02-015) is not a new formula. Load `MemberFinancials` and every `MemberFinancialsSnapshot` for the members, then for each applicable holiday call `resolveRateAtDate(snapshots, live, holiday.date)` and `buildHolidayRow(holiday, member, rate.billRate)` from `packages/validation` — exactly what apps/api/src/reports/reports.service.ts:785-812 does — and sum `Number(row.amount)`. That per-row `toMoney` rounding, summed afterwards, is what the report produces; computing an unrounded sum instead makes TC-02-INT-09's cent-exact comparison fail on a fixture with an odd rate.

A member with no `MemberFinancials` row: `amount` and `currency` are ABSENT keys — not null, not zero — and the member contributes nothing to `byCurrency`, while `holidayCount` and `paidHours` are reported exactly as for anybody else (REQ-02-018, REQ-02-024). Note that `resolveRateAtDate` returns a billRate of 0 for such a member, so absence must be decided by the missing financials row, never by a zero amount.

`currency` comes from the member's live `MemberFinancials.currency`. `totals.byCurrency` is one entry per distinct currency, each summing only its own members; there is no total across currencies anywhere in the body (REQ-02-016).

`totals.holidayCount` and `totals.paidHours` are summed OVER MEMBERS, which is what TC-02-INT-08 asserts and what the §Screens mock shows (37 days across three members). The sample body in the contracts file totals 24 there; see the note in `risks`.

Without `view-amounts-owed`: every `amount` and `currency` key is absent from every member row and `byCurrency` is absent from `totals` (REQ-02-017) — omitted, never zeroed, so the shape of the body says nothing about what was withheld.
Every query scopes by `session.organizationId`.

premises.claim: migrations run on the new image BEFORE the Terraform rollout, which is why additive is the rule
Holiday already carries @@unique([organizationId, date, countryCode]), so a concurrent duplicate insert collides rather than duplicating
Membership.countryCode and Organization.countryCode both exist and are nullable — time off 01 shipped them
the Amounts Owed report values a holiday at paidHours x the rate in force on its date, rounding each row to the cent before summing

can() does not normalize — CAPABILITY_MATRIX['member'] is undefined and every capability comes back false, so a new check must call can(normalizeRole(role), …)
the mail port defaults to its local driver whenever NODE_ENV is not production, which is the idiom the contracts file calls the house pattern
an abstract class is used as the DI token and the driver is chosen in a factory at module construction
Node's global fetch has no timeout; the repository bounds an outbound call with an AbortController and a cleared timer
every design-system component the screen needs already exports from the package root — Card, Button, Checkbox, InfoBanner, Preloader, ReportTableHead, ReportGroupBody
the E2E preconditions all ship — member country, organization country, holiday, financials, snapshot backdating, role change
the integration suite can swap a provider for a double through overrideProvider on the abstract-class token

risks.risk: REQ-02-013 says a country row carries 'the number of holidays stored for it', and the spec never says whether a global holiday (countryCode null) counts toward a country. The cases seed none, so both readings pass TC-02-INT-08.
risks.mitigation: Planned as: a holiday counts toward a country when isHolidayApplicableToMember would apply it — its countryCode is null or equal. That is the one applicability rule this area already has, and it is the only reading under which a country's row and its members' rows on the same screen agree. Recorded as note P2.

risks.risk: The contracts sample body totals holidayCount 24 (13 + 11, the country sum) while TC-02-INT-08 says the total is the sum over members and the §Screens mock shows 37 across three members.
risks.mitigation: Planned as the sum over members. The sample is arithmetically inconsistent with its own countries array (PL memberCount 2 with one PL member shown), so it is illustrative of shape; the case and the mock agree with each other. Recorded as note P3.

risks.risk: The contracts prose says the holidays array is unchanged in shape and that the response gains one field, while the same file's sample row carries `source` and the testid table requires holidays-row-{id}-source per row.
risks.mitigation: Planned as: the array gains `source` and loses nothing, because no other route can tell the screen where a row came from. Recorded as note P4.

risks.risk: GET .../holidays?scope=mine needs no capability. Adding the sourcing block unconditionally would hand a user or a viewer the organization's country set and its import state.
risks.mitigation: Planned as: sourcing is present only on a read that passed the view-holidays gate. The spec's §Security states a capability per question and REQ-02-019 gates the sourcing state, so this is the reading consistent with both; the screen always reads scope=all. Recorded as note P5.

risks.risk: A global manual holiday and an imported national holiday can both land on one date: REQ-02-006 keys the skip on date AND country, and the unique index treats a null countryCode as distinct. Both then apply to the same member, and Amounts Owed pays both.
risks.mitigation: Planned exactly as REQ-02-006 states — the rule is unambiguous — with the consequence recorded as note P6 for a human to decide later. Do not invent a wider skip rule: that would change what the decision table says about a manual row on the same date.

risks.risk: REQ-02-015's equality with the report is fragile: the report rounds each holiday row to the cent (buildHolidayRow returns a toMoney string) and sums afterwards. An unrounded sum diverges on fixtures with an odd rate and TC-02-INT-09 fails.
risks.mitigation: T5 calls the same two exported functions and sums Number(row.amount), so the arithmetic is not reproduced but reused.

risks.risk: A country the provider never covers (India) keeps its unsourced state forever, so REQ-02-012 issues a sync on every page load and pays the call bound each time.
risks.mitigation: Named in Known Gaps and bounded by invariant 5; the screen issues at most one sync per load and shows the uncovered warning. Do not add a retry, a backoff or a negative-cache table — that is a spec of its own.

risks.risk: The verification plan was never walked (Known Gaps), so no step of the rig is proven and the fake driver, the capability-free summary method and the role that separates the two money capabilities are the three preconditions that do not exist yet.
risks.mitigation: T3 builds the fake, T5 splits the summary method so TC-02-INT-11 can drive it, and the Known Gap accepts that no role separates the capabilities. Each is a task, which is what the cases file asks for.

risks.risk: Nothing in Terraform names the three HOLIDAY_PROVIDER* variables, so a deployed environment runs the nager driver on its built-in defaults.
risks.mitigation: That is what the spec intends — none of the three is a secret and each carries a default — and no requirement asks for an infrastructure change. Left out of the plan deliberately; the .env.example rows document the choice.
